w:r.w:t: User Identity, Session Lifecycle, Route Protection, Internal Auth, Ownership, Expiry, and Security Boundaries

This document defines Authentication and Session Management for Torgima Phase 1. It specifies how users sign in, how sessions are created and validated, how route access is protected, how user ownership is enforced, how sessions expire, and how internal system routes are protected from client access.

Authentication proves who is making a request. Authorization and the Control Engine decide what that user may do. This document handles identity and session validity; it does not replace the permission and control systems.
Rule: No user-facing state, task, feedback, blueprint, reward, identity, or outcome data may be read or mutated without a valid session and ownership check.
Authentication confirms identity. Sessions preserve identity. Ownership limits identity.
A valid login is not permission to access everything. Every request must connect the authenticated user to the requested resource and route class.

5. What This System Does Not Own
It does not decide whether an authenticated user may perform every action; authorization and Control Engine handle action permission.
It does not validate feedback, outcomes, tasks, or signals.
It does not store raw passwords unless a local auth provider is explicitly implemented with hashing.
It does not expose internal route tokens to the browser.
It does not bypass state versioning, idempotency, or enforcement packages.
Do not build team permission complexity into Phase 1 UI.

Authentication is the front gate of Torgima, but not the whole control system. It proves who the user is, keeps the session valid, protects resources by ownership, and blocks unsafe access. Once identity is confirmed, authorization, state versioning, and the Control Engine decide what can happen next.
